Rashi on Zevachim 10a:10:1.hebrew: שחט לשם פלוני כשר - דאין שינוי בעלים חל על השחיטה, דלא שייך שם בעלים אלא על הכפרה. והיינו דאמרן לעיל (זבחים דף ד.) דשינוי בעלים אינו בד' עבודות:
Rashi on Zevachim 10a:10:1.english: If he slaughtered it for the sake of so-and-so, it is fit - For a deviation with regard to the owner does not take effect on the slaughter, since the term "owner" is relevant only to the atonement. And this is what we said above (Zevachim 4a), that a deviation with regard to the owner does not apply to the four [sacrificial] services.

Rashi on Zevachim 10a:11:1.hebrew: לא תאמר בזריקה - מחשבין מעבודה לעבודה שלא לשמו, דרבינן ליה לעיל בכולהו עבודות:
Rashi on Zevachim 10a:11:1.english: Do not say [that the requirement of 'for its own sake' is written] with regard to sprinkling - [that one may] have intention from one rite to another [to offer it] not for its own sake, [for] we derived it above for all the rites:

Rashi on Zevachim 10a:11:2.hebrew: משחיטה וקבלה - ומה שחיטה, שכשרה בזר, פסולה בשלא לשמה — זריקה, לא כל שכן? כי פרכת: מה לשחיטה, שכן פוסלת שלא לשם אוכלין בפסח! קבלה תוכיח:
Rashi on Zevachim 10a:11:2.english: From slaughter and collection - Just as slaughter, which is valid when performed by a non-priest, is invalid when done not for its own sake, then sprinkling, all the more so! If you refute this: What is true of slaughter is that it invalidates [the offering] when done for the sake of [a different type of] eaters in the case of the Paschal offering! Collection proves otherwise.

Rashi on Zevachim 10a:11:3.hebrew: דאין מחשבין מעבודה לעבודה - אלא בשעת זריקה גופה בעי מיחשב:
Rashi on Zevachim 10a:11:3.english: That one cannot have intention from one rite to another - Rather, specifically at the time of the sprinkling itself, one must have the [proper] intention.

Rashi on Zevachim 10a:12:1.hebrew: ודלמא - להכי כתביה לאשמועינן רבותא דמחשבין מעבודה לעבודה, [שלא] בשעת זריקה גופה בעי מחשב, דאפי' לא חישב על הזריקה בשעתה אלא בשעת שחיטה הויא מחשבה:
Rashi on Zevachim 10a:12:1.english: But perhaps - For this reason [the verse] wrote it: to teach us the novelty that one may have intention from one rite to another rite, [so that] he need not intend [the improper thought] at the time of the sprinkling itself; for even if he did not think about the sprinkling at its proper time, but [only] at the time of the slaughter, it is [a valid disqualifying] thought.

Rashi on Zevachim 10a:13:1.hebrew: אם כן - דמחשבין אתא לאשמועינן, לשתוק קרא מיניה, ותיתי דמחשבין מקל וחומר דרב אשי כדאמרן: ומה אם במקום שאם אמר הריני שוחט לשם פלוני כו':
Rashi on Zevachim 10a:13:1.english: If so - If the verse came to teach us [the law] of intentions, let the verse be silent about it, and [the law] of intentions would come [to be derived] from the a fortiori argument of Rav Ashi, as we said: "And if in a case where, if he said, 'I am slaughtering for the sake of so-and-so,' etc."

Rashi on Zevachim 10a:14:1.hebrew: ואידך - רבי יוחנן פריך הכי, דלא נפקא לן זריקה מקל וחומר דקבלה ושחיטה:
Rashi on Zevachim 10a:14:1.english: And the other - Rabbi Yochanan refutes it this way: that we cannot derive sprinkling by a kal vachomer from receiving [the blood] and slaughtering.

Rashi on Zevachim 10a:14:2.hebrew: מה להנך כו' - הלכך לאו קרא יתירא הוא דניליף מיניה דאין מחשבין:
Rashi on Zevachim 10a:14:2.english: What about these, etc. - Therefore, it is not an extra verse from which we derive that [the Torah teaches that] one does not render [the offering] invalid through improper intent:

Rashi on Zevachim 10a:15:1.hebrew: השתא מיהת בשלמים קיימינן - דבשלמים כתיבא מחשבה שלא לשמו, הלכך מצי למילף זריקה משחיטה וקבלה. וליכא למיפרך "צפון", דשלמים לא בעי צפון; וליתנהו "פנימיות":
Rashi on Zevachim 10a:15:1.english: Now, in any event, we stand with regard to peace offerings - For with regard to peace offerings, [the law of] a thought to offer them not for their own sake is written; therefore, one can derive [the law of] sprinkling from slaughter and receiving. And one cannot refute [this derivation by arguing] "north," since peace offerings do not require [slaughter in the] north; nor [by arguing] "inner [sin offerings]," since they are not [offered with blood brought] inside.

Rashi on Zevachim 10a:18:1.hebrew: שכן דמה למעלה - מחוט הסיקרא, דתנן במס' מדות (פ"ג מ"א): חוט הסיקרא חוגרת באמצע להבדיל בין דמים עליונים לדמים התחתונים. ויליף לקמן (זבחים דף נג.) מן והיתה הרשת עד חצי המזבח, התורה נתנה מחיצה להבדיל. וחטאת בהמה נעשית למעלה, דכתיב בה (ויקרא ד) על קרנות, וכן עולת העוף, כדלקמן (זבחים דף סד:). ושאר זבחים שלא פירש בהן נעשין למטה, דכתיב בהו מזבח ולא כתיב בהו קרנות. וכוליה מזבח ליכא למימר דהוה מקומן, שהרי תורה נתנה מחיצה:
Rashi on Zevachim 10a:18:1.english: For its blood is above - Above the thread of red paint (the sikra line), as we learned in tractate Middot (3:1): The thread of red paint encircles [the altar] at its middle, to separate between the upper blood and the lower blood. And [the Gemara] derives this below (Zevachim 53a) from [the verse], "And the net shall be up to the middle of the altar" — the Torah established a partition in order to separate. The sin offering of an animal is performed above, as it is written regarding it (Leviticus 4), "on the horns," and so too the bird burnt offering, as [stated] below (Zevachim 64b). But the other offerings, regarding which [the Torah] did not specify, are performed below, as it is written regarding them "the altar" and it is not written regarding them "horns." And it cannot be said that their place is the entire altar, since the Torah established a partition.

Rashi on Zevachim 10a:19:1.hebrew: פסח יוכיח: שדמו למטה, כדאמרינן במתניתין, ועל זה פריך במתניתין דמה לפסח שכן זמנו קבוע:

Rashi on Zevachim 10a:1:1.hebrew: השוחט את הבהמה - הבהמה של חולין לעבודת כוכבים, אסורה בהנאה כדין זבחי מתים. וזבחי מתים ילפינן (ע"ז דף כט:) "שם שם" מעגלה ערופה:
Rashi on Zevachim 10a:1:1.english: One who slaughters the animal - an unconsecrated animal for idol worship, it is prohibited for benefit, like the law of sacrifices of the dead. And we derive the law of sacrifices of the dead (Avodah Zarah 29b) from a verbal analogy of "there… there" from the heifer whose neck is broken.

Rashi on Zevachim 10a:1:2.hebrew: לזרוק דמה לעבודת כוכבים - (ועבודת) השחיטה לא נעשית לשם עבודת כוכבים, אלא בשעת שחיטה חישב לעבוד הזריקה לשם עבודת כוכבים, ולא זרק:
Rashi on Zevachim 10a:1:2.english: To sprinkle its blood for idol worship - The slaughter was not performed for the sake of idol worship. Rather, at the time of slaughter he intended to perform the sprinkling for the sake of idol worship, but he did not sprinkle.

Rashi on Zevachim 10a:1:3.hebrew: מחשבין מעבודה לעבודה - מחשבה היא לענין זבחי מתים, ליאסר בהנאה:
Rashi on Zevachim 10a:1:3.english: One can have intention from one rite to another - It is [considered] an intention with regard to sacrifices of the dead [i.e., idolatrous offerings], so that [the animal] becomes prohibited for benefit.

Rashi on Zevachim 10a:1:4.hebrew: דילפינן - עבודת כוכבים, שהיא חוץ, ממחשבת פיגול, שהוא פנים:
Rashi on Zevachim 10a:1:4.english: We derive - [the law of] idol worship, which is [applicable] outside [the Temple], from [the law of] the intent of piggul, which is [applicable] inside [the Temple].

Rashi on Zevachim 10a:20:1.hebrew: מה לפסח: שכן זמנו קבוע לאשם דלית ליה זמן קבוע:

Rashi on Zevachim 10a:21:1.hebrew: חטאת תוכיח: דלית ליה זמן קבוע ופסולה שלא לשמה ודמה למעלה:

Rashi on Zevachim 10a:2:2.hebrew: אין מחשבין מעבודה לעבודה - ואינה אסורה אלא אם כן שחט לעבודת כוכבים, שבשחיטתה עבד עבודת כוכבים, או זרק לעבודת כוכבים:
Rashi on Zevachim 10a:2:2.english: One does not have intention from one rite to another - And [the animal] is not forbidden unless he slaughtered it for idol worship, such that through its slaughter he performed idol worship, or he sprinkled [its blood] for idol worship:

Rashi on Zevachim 10a:3:1.hebrew: פנים מפנים - ילפינן מחשבת שלא לשמו מפיגול:
Rashi on Zevachim 10a:3:1.english: Inside from inside - [We derive] the [law of] intention of not for its own sake from [the law of] piggul.

Rashi on Zevachim 10a:6:1.hebrew: הריני שוחט חוץ לזמנו - ולא חישב על מנת לאכול, ולא על מנת לזרוק או להקטיר, אלא על השחיטה חישב סתם חוץ לזמנה — כשר, דלאו מחשבה היא, דאין זמן אלא באכילת אדם ומזבח, (דזהו) שהוא פיגול:
Rashi on Zevachim 10a:6:1.english: I am hereby slaughtering it beyond its time - And he did not intend to eat, nor to sprinkle or to burn [it on the altar]; rather, he merely intended, with respect to the slaughter itself, [that it be done] beyond its time — [the offering] is fit, because this is not [a legally operative] thought, since "time" applies only to eating by a person and [eating by] the altar, which is [the matter of] piggul.

Rashi on Zevachim 10a:7:1.hebrew: שכן כרת - האוכל פיגול, אפי' לאלתר, חייב כרת, הואיל וחמור. ולכן מהניא ביה מחשבה מעבודה לעבודה:
Rashi on Zevachim 10a:7:1.english: For it entails karet - One who eats piggul, even immediately, is liable to karet, since it is severe. [Therefore] intent is effective in it from one service to another.

Rashi on Zevachim 10a:8:1.hebrew: הריני שוחטו חוץ למקומו - שלא חישב לא על אכילה ולא על זריקה, אלא אמר: הריני שוחט חוץ למקומו — כשר, דהא חזינן דבמקומו הוא שוחטו. ועוד, דבאכילת אדם או מזבח תלה רחמנא לחוץ למקומו וחוץ לזמנו, דכתיב "ואם האכל יאכל" וגו', וילפינן חוץ למקומו וחוץ לזמנו מהאי קרא לקמן (זבחים דף יג.):
Rashi on Zevachim 10a:8:1.english: I am hereby slaughtering it outside its place - Meaning, he did not have in mind either eating or sprinkling, but [merely] said, "I am hereby slaughtering outside its place" — [the offering] is fit, for we see that he is in fact slaughtering it in its [proper] place. Furthermore, the Merciful One made [the disqualification of] "outside its place" and "outside its time" dependent on eating, by a person or by the altar, as it is written, "And if any of the flesh … shall be eaten" etc., and we derive "outside its place" and "outside its time" from this verse later (Zevachim 13a).

Rashi on Zevachim 10a:8:2.hebrew: על מנת לזרוק דמו חוץ למקומו כו' פסול - (בפרק שני) והשתא ליכא למפרך "שכן כרת", שאין חייבין כרת על אכילתן, כדתניא לקמן [בפרק שני] (דף כח.):
Rashi on Zevachim 10a:8:2.english: [If he slaughtered] in order to sprinkle its blood outside its area, etc., it is unfit - (in the second chapter) And now there is no room to object, "[No,] since it involves karet," for one is not liable to karet for eating them, as is taught below [in the second chapter] (28a).

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:25:1.hebrew: שחטה לשמה - שלא חישב על השחיטה אלא על הזריקה חישב בשעת שחיטה, דהיינו מעבודה לעבודה:
Rashi on Zevachim 9b:25:1.english: He slaughtered it for its sake – meaning that he did not intend for the slaughter itself, but rather he intended for the sprinkling of the blood at the time of the slaughter; this is an example of (intent transferring) from one sacrificial rite to another sacrificial rite.

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:26:1.hebrew: מחשבין מעבודה לעבודה - כלומר מחשבה מועלת מעבודה לעבודה במחשבת שלא לשמו:
Rashi on Zevachim 9b:26:1.english: One can have intention from rite to rite – meaning that an improper intention is effective (to disqualify the offering) even if it pertains to one rite (e.g., slaughter) but is related to a subsequent rite (e.g., sprinkling the blood) with the intention of *shelo lishma* (not for its sake).

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:27:1.hebrew: אין מחשבין מעבודה לעבודה - בשלא לשמו דלא ילפינן לה מפיגול. דהתם עיקר מחשבתו המביאה לידי פיגול זו היא שיחשוב בעבודה זו לעשות עבודה אחרת מן אחת העבודות להאכיל לאדם או למזבח חוץ לזמנו, וזריקה אכילת מזבח היא, והוא הדין אם חישב על הקטרת החלב שאינה מן עבודות. הילכך לא דמיא לשלא לשמו:
Rashi on Zevachim 9b:27:1.english: One cannot have intention from rite to rite – (this applies) to *shelo lishma* (not for its sake), for we do not derive it from *piggul*. For there (in the case of *piggul*), the primary intention that leads to *piggul* is to intend during one rite to perform another act of Temple service for the purpose of feeding a person or the altar beyond its designated time. Sprinkling is considered 'consumption by the altar.' The same applies if he intended to burn the forbidden fat, which is also an act of consumption by the altar. Therefore, this *piggul* mechanism is not similar to the (mere) intention of *shelo lishma* (not for its sake, and thus *shelo lishma* intent does not transfer between rites).

Tosafot on Zevachim 10a:10:1.hebrew: מקום שאם אמר הריני שוחט שלא לשמן כו' - וא"ת: שוחט שלא לשם אוכלין בפסח יוכיח, דשוחט שלא לשם אוכלין פסול, ושוחט ע"מ לזרוק שלא לשם אוכלין כשר! ויש לומר: דלא דמי, התם דזורק עצמו שלא לשם אוכלין כשר:
Tosafot on Zevachim 10a:10:1.english: "A case where, if he said 'I am slaughtering not for their sake' etc." - And if you ask: Let the Paschal offering serve as a counter-proof! For if one slaughters it not for the sake of those who will eat it, it is unfit, yet if one slaughters it with the intention to sprinkle its blood not for the sake of those who will eat it, it is fit! And one can answer: It is not comparable, since there, [in the case of the Paschal offering,] the sprinkling itself, if done not for the sake of those who will eat it, is fit.

Tosafot on Zevachim 10a:11:1.hebrew: לא תאמר בזריקה ותיתי בק"ו משחיטה וקבלה - תימה: אמאי לא פריך "שכן טעונות צפון, וישנן בחטאות הפנימיות"? וכ"ת משום דבשלמים קיימא — אם כן מאי צריך למילף מבינייא? ניליף בק"ו מקבלה, שאין חייבין עליה בחוץ, ואפילו הכי פסלה בה מחשבה. ועוד: למה לי קרא בזריקה לשינוי בעלים, דדרשי' "לכפר עליו"? תיתי מבינייא משחיטה וקבלה. ועוד קשה: אמאי אין מחשבת אוכלין בפסח בזריקה? תיתי בק"ו משחיטה, שכשירה בזר, כיון דלא פרכינן מצפון וחטאות הפנימיות. ומיהו דילמא (תכוסו) מיעוטא הוא, ואע"ג דשלא למנויין, דהיינו שינוי בעלים, כתיב נמי (תכוסו), ולא ממעטי זריקה — לא דמי (עיין פסחים דף סא.):
Tosafot on Zevachim 10a:11:1.english: "You should not say regarding sprinkling, for it would be derived by an a fortiori inference from slaughter and collection" - This is puzzling: Why does one not refute [the inference] by saying, "Since they require [being done in] the north, and they exist in the inner sin offerings"? And if you say [this refutation does not apply] because [the verse] is dealing with peace offerings — if so, why is it necessary to derive it from the common element? Let us derive it by an a fortiori inference from collection, which one is not liable for [doing] outside [the Temple], and nevertheless intention disqualifies it. Furthermore: Why do I need a verse regarding sprinkling for a change of owner, which we expound from "to atone for him"? Let it be derived from the common element of slaughter and collection. Furthermore, it is difficult: Why is the intention of those eating the Pesach offering not [effective] with regard to sprinkling? Let it be derived by an a fortiori inference from slaughter, which is valid when done by a non-priest, since we do not refute [the inference] from the requirement of the north and the inner sin offerings. However, perhaps "(you shall be counted)" is a limiting term; and although "not for those counted" — which is a change of owner — is also written with "(you shall be counted)", and they do not exclude sprinkling — it is not comparable (see Pesachim 61a).

Tosafot on Zevachim 10a:16:1.hebrew: והדר ביה רבה לגבי דרב נחמן מקל וחומר דרב אשי - [היינו] לרבנן, דאליבא דר' שמעון ליכא קל וחומר, דאיכא למיפרך: מה לשינוי בעלים, שכן נוהג במנחות; תאמר בשינוי קודש, שאינו נוהג במנחות לרבי שמעון (מנחות דף ב:):
Tosafot on Zevachim 10a:16:1.english: "And Rabba retracted his opinion in favor of Rav Nachman, due to Rav Ashi's a fortiori inference" - [That is,] according to the Rabbis; for according to Rabbi Shimon there is no a fortiori inference, since one can refute it: What [proof is there] from a change of owner's intent, which applies also to meal offerings? Would you say the same of a change of the sacrifice's designation, which, according to Rabbi Shimon, does not apply to meal offerings? (Menachot 2b).

Tosafot on Zevachim 10a:2:1.hebrew: ריש לקיש אמר מותרת - מודה ר"ל דחייב מיתה, כדאמרינן בפרק ארבע מיתות (סנהדרין סא.): מידי דהוה אמשתחוה להר, דהר מותר ועובדו בסייף. ושחיטת מומר לא חשיב, כדפי' בפ"ק דחולין (דף יד.) גבי שוחט בשבת. ואין לתמוה והיאך נהרג, דילמא מימלך ולא זריק לעבודת כוכבים, כדאמר בפרק ד' מיתות (סנהדרין סא.) דניסת שאמר אלך אעבוד פטור, דמימלך ולא עביד — דהכא ודאי לא מימלך, כיון דעבד מעשה ששחט על מנת לזרוק. ועוד, הכא אפילו ידוע ודאי שלא יזרוק, חשיב עובד עבודת כוכבים בשחיטה [[זו] כששוחט ע"מ לזרוק:
Tosafot on Zevachim 10a:2:1.english: Reish Lakish says: It is permitted - Reish Lakish agrees that [the one who slaughters for idolatry] is liable to death, as we say in the chapter [of] "Arba Mitot" (Sanhedrin 61a): It is like one who bows down to a mountain, where the mountain is permitted but the one who worships it is [executed] by the sword. And the slaughter of an apostate is not considered [a valid slaughter], as I explained in the first chapter of Chullin (14a) regarding one who slaughters on Shabbat. And one should not wonder how he is put to death — perhaps he will change his mind and not throw [the blood] to the idol, as stated in the chapter "Arba Mitot" (Sanhedrin 61a) that one who says "I will go and worship" is exempt, since he may change his mind and not do it. Here, certainly he did not change his mind, since he performed an act, slaughtering with the intention to throw. Furthermore, here even if it is known for certain that he will not throw, he is considered one who worships idolatry through slaughter, [this being so] when he slaughters with the intention to throw.

Tosafot on Zevachim 9b:26:1.hebrew: מחשבין מעבודה לעבודה - כדאמר, כגון משחיטה לזריקה (כמו שינוי בעלים), אבל משחיטה לקבלה לא, דהא מפיגול ילפינן לה, וקל וחומר דרב אשי דילפינן משינוי בעלים לא הוי אלא משחיטה לזריקה, כמו שינוי בעלים. ותימה, דלקמן (זבחים דף יג.) דפריך: וקבלה מי פסלה כו', ומשני: כאן במחשבת שלא לשמן, כאן במחשבת פיגול. אמאי לא משני: אידי ואידי במחשבת שלא לשמן, וקבלה לא עשה בה מחשבה כמעשה, כגון בשוחט על מנת לקבל שלא לשמן? ובזריקה (גם) עשה בה מחשבה כמעשה? ונראה לי דלקמן מיירי שחישב בעבודה עצמה: אם קיבל לגמור הקבלה שלא לשמן - פסול. ואם קיבל לגמור חוץ לזמנו - כשר. ואם זרק לגמור הזריקה חוץ לזמנו - פסול. וכן מקטיר לגמור ההקטרה למחר - דהוה פסול, אי לאו דמעטיה קרא לקמן משום דאין מעכבת כפרה. אבל ליכא לפרושי לקמן מחשבת פיגול דלא פסלה בקבלה כגון שוחט על מנת לקבל דמן חוץ לזמנו, דבשלא לשמן נמי לא פסלה, דמעבודה לעבודה ילפינן מפיגול. (ואי) במקבל על מנת לזרוק חוץ לזמנו - הוה פיגול, אלא כדפרשינן בחישב בעבודה עצמה. ברוך. ובלאו הכי תימה דהוי מצי למימר: קבלה לא עשה בה מחשבה כמעשה לענין שינוי בעלים:
Tosafot on Zevachim 9b:26:1.english: One can have intention from rite to rite – as stated (by Rabbi Yochanan), for example, (the intention passes) from slaughter to sprinkling (as in change of owners), but not from slaughter to receiving (the blood). For this (idea of intent transferring) is derived from *piggul*. And the *kal va'chomer* (a fortiori inference) of Rav Ashi, which is derived from a change of owners, applies only from slaughter to sprinkling, similar to a change of owners. And it is difficult, for later (Zevachim 13a) it is asked: 'And does collection (with improper intent) disqualify, etc.?' And it answers: 'Here (the mishna refers to) *shelo lishma* (not for its sake) intent, there (the *baraita* refers to) *piggul* intent.' Why doesn't it answer: 'Both (the mishna and *baraita*) refer to *shelo lishma* intent, and collection (of the blood) does not treat intention as action,' for example, in one who slaughters with intent to receive (the blood) not for its sake? And in sprinkling, it *does* treat intention as action? And it seems to me that later (Zevachim 13a) it deals with one who intended during the rite itself: if he received (the blood) to complete the receiving not for its sake – it is disqualified. And if he received (the blood) to complete (the receiving) beyond its time – it is fit. And if he sprinkled to complete the sprinkling beyond its time – it is disqualified. And similarly, if he burned to complete the burning on the next day – it would be disqualified, if not for the verse that explicitly limits it later, because it (the burning of *eimurim*) does not prevent atonement. But it is not possible to explain later that *piggul* intent does not disqualify during collection, for example, if one slaughters with intent to receive its blood beyond its time. For even for *shelo lishma* it does not disqualify, as 'from rite to rite' we derive from *piggul*. (And if) one collects with intent to sprinkle beyond its time – it would be *piggul*, rather, as we explained, (it refers to) intending during the rite itself. Blessed (be God). And even without this, it is difficult, for it could have said: collection does not treat intention as action with regard to change of owners.

Zevachim 10a:17.english: The mishna teaches: Rabbi Eliezer says: The guilt offering, too, is unfit when sacrificed not for its sake. With regard to this [matter of the guilt offering] it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Eliezer said: A sin offering is brought for committing a transgression and a guilt offering is brought for committing a transgression. Just as a sin offering sacrificed not for its sake is unfit, so too, a guilt offering sacrificed not for its sake is unfit.

Zevachim 10a:18.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to Rabbi Eliezer: The inference is not valid. If you say this with regard to a sin offering, whose blood is sprinkled above the red line that encircles the altar, should you necessarily say the same with regard to a guilt offering, whose blood is sprinkled below that line, like most animal offerings?

Zevachim 10a:19.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to Rabbi Yehoshua: A Paschal offering can prove the point, as its blood is sprinkled below the red line (on the lower half of the altar), and nevertheless, if one slaughtered it not for its sake it is unfit.

Zevachim 10a:20.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to Rabbi Eliezer: What is notable about a Paschal offering? It is notable in that its designated time is fixed. A guilt offering does not have a fixed time.

Zevachim 10a:21.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to Rabbi Yehoshua: A sin offering can prove the point, as it does not have a fixed time, and nevertheless, it is disqualified if sacrificed not for its sake.

Zevachim 10a:22.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to Rabbi Eliezer: I return to my previous claim that a sin offering is unique since its blood is sprinkled above the red line.
